resources.string: Auto-connect to a harness found on Wi-Fi
Reconnect to the last harness you used
Auto-connect to the harness on this device
Auto-connect to a paired relay on Wi-Fi
Start the harness in Termux when the app opens
Only if it isn't already running, and only after you've allowed Termux commands.
No harnesses found yet. Check that the harness is running and your phone is on the same Wi-Fi.

%1$s showed a different key from the one saved when this device paired. This happens when a relay makes a new certificate after moving networks, but it looks the same as something else answering at that address. Pair again only if you expected this.
Nothing on this network answers to “%1$s”. Use the computer's IP address instead. To find it, run ipconfig on Windows, ip addr on Linux, or ifconfig on macOS.
Enter the computer's IP address and a port between 1 and 65535.
Something answered at %1$s, but it isn't a DeepSeek Harness. Check the port the harness printed at startup.
The relay no longer accepts this device's token. It may have expired or been removed from the relay's device list. Pair again to get a new one.
%1$s refused the connection. The harness only listens on the computer itself unless LAN mode is on. Turn it on and restart the harness. If you changed the port, check that it matches.
The relay at %1$s accepted this device, but the harness behind it refused the relay's sign-in. Pairing again won't help. Update dsh-relay on that computer and restart dsh web.

%1$s answered, but its event stream wouldn't open. A VPN or private-DNS proxy on this phone can block WebSocket connections. Turn it off and try again. Android can also freeze the app right after launch. If so, force-stop the app and try again.
%1$s isn't on this phone's network. This phone is on %2$s. Connect both devices to the same router network. Guest and IoT Wi-Fi are usually kept separate, and Scan network only searches %2$s.
Nothing answered at %1$s. The computer's firewall is probably blocking incoming connections on port %2$d. Allow it and try again. Some routers also stop Wi-Fi devices from reaching wired ones.

%1$s answered, but the secure (HTTPS) connection failed. If your proxy uses a local certificate authority, install its CA certificate on this phone. If the address doesn't serve HTTPS, connect without https://.
%1$s is a harness, but it hasn't signed this phone in. Open the harness startup link on this device once, then connect again.
Use the computer's IP address instead of its name, or start the harness with --trusted-host.
A harness is running here but refuses requests from this device. Restart it with --trusted-host for this phone.
Mirror the harness running on your computer.
Not encrypted. Use Local network only on Wi-Fi you trust.
Runs the harness in Termux on this phone. DSH can start, stop and sign in for you.
The agent keeps working on the computer. Your draft and place in each chat are saved.
Paste the link dsh web prints, token included, and you'll be signed in too.
No relays found yet. Install the dsh-relay plugin in the harness web profile, restart it, then look again.
Encrypted and password-protected. Scan the pairing QR from dsh-relay.
A relay is running here, but it only answers to addresses it already knows. Add %1$s to publicHostnames in the relay's cordis.patch.yml on that computer, then restart it.
Relays you pair with appear here.
Harnesses you connect to appear here.
The harness prints a link when it starts. Paste the link, or only the token after ?token=.
Try connecting first, then sign in.
The harness didn't accept that token. It changes on every restart, so check the latest startup line.
This harness hasn't signed this phone in yet.
The token changes every time the harness restarts.
Couldn't reach the harness to sign in.
